name: Elektorornis
sum: Cenomanian enantiornithean from Burmese amber with a remarkably long third toe.
holotype: A partial hindlimb and some wing feathers in amber (number in Xing et al. 2019).
biology: The elongated toe may have been used to pull food from tree crevices (Xing et al. 2019); Clark et al. (2021) discussed the interpretation.
author: Xing et al. 2019
